name: Recipe
description: 'How an output is made: a `command` and the compute `resources` it asks
  for. What the output is made from and the decisions it is made with are the output''s
  `inputs` and `decisions`; the command reaches the inputs and decisions through its
  placeholders.'
from_schema: https://w3id.org/astra/analysis
attributes:
  command:
    name: command
    description: "The POSIX shell command that makes the output, such as `python src/output1.py`.\
      \ It is a template. Read from the left, `{{` stands for a literal `{` and `}}`\
      \ for a literal `}`, and any other `{` opens a placeholder, which ends at the\
      \ next `}`. A runner substitutes each placeholder, and each `{{` and `}}`, before\
      \ running the command:\n\n  {inputs.<entry>}     the path of what an entry of\
      \ the output's\n                       `inputs` names (for a switch, what the\
      \ case\n                       it takes names), with <entry> written\n     \
      \                  exactly as the entry is, dots and `#`\n                 \
      \      included, as in\n                       {inputs.subanalysis.output1#u1}\n\
      \  {decisions.<entry>}  the id of the option selected for the\n            \
      \           decision an entry of the output's\n                       `decisions`\
      \ names, with <entry> written\n                       exactly as the entry is,\
      \ as in\n                       {decisions.subanalysis.decision1}\n  {inputs}\
      \             the paths of all the output's inputs, in\n                   \
      \    the order of `inputs`, separated by spaces\n  {output}             the\
      \ path the result is written to\n\nEvery brace belongs to a `{{`, a `}}` or\
      \ a placeholder, every placeholder takes one of these forms, and the <entry>\
      \ of an {inputs.<entry>} or {decisions.<entry>} is an entry of the output's\
      \ `inputs` or `decisions`, exactly as written."
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/astra/analysis
    rank: 1000
    owner: Recipe
    domain_of:
    - Recipe
    range: string
    required: true
  resources:
    name: resources
    description: Compute resource requirements (cpus, memory, time_limit, …)

    rank: 1000

items.title: Type: Uri
items.text: a complete URI

items.title: Type: Uriorcurie
items.text: a URI or a CURIE

items.title: Slot: address
items.text: The result's address, as the analysis it belongs to names it: the output's id after the ids of the driven declarations that lead to it, then, for a result built in a universe, # and that universe's own id, never an import's, such as subanalysis.output1#u1.

items.title: Slot: analyses
items.text: The analyses this analysis uses, keyed by the id it addresses them by.

items.title: Slot: analysis
items.text: For an import, the address of the declaration that leads to the analysis whose universe it imports, through as many declarations as lead to it, such as subanalysis or stage.inner.

items.title: Slot: artifact
items.text: A reference to the cited output, written as in an output's inputs. It may pin the output to a universe, the one the claim is about, such as output1#u1. A switch is cited as the case it takes, and each of its cases names an output other than a switch, or a switch like it.

items.title: Slot: case
items.text: The id of an option of the switch's decision, written as its key in cases.

items.title: Slot: cases
items.text: For a switch, what it is read as where its decision selects each option that has a case, as <option>: <reference>, such as b: stage.output3. There is at least one, and several options can name one reference. Where its decision selects an option with no case, the switch isn't built, nor is anything that reads it without a pin.

items.title: Slot: claim
items.text: What the insight asserts.

items.title: Slot: command
items.text:
The POSIX shell command that makes the output, such as python src/output1.py. It is a template. Read from the left, {{ stands for a literal { and }} for a literal }, and any other { opens a placeholder, which ends at the next }. A runner substitutes each placeholder, and each {{ and }}, before running the command:

__

_ {inputs.<entry>} the path of what an entry of the output's_

_ inputs names (for a switch, what the case_

_ it takes names), with <entry> written_

_ exactly as the entry is, dots and #_

_ included, as in_

_ {inputs.subanalysis.output1#u1}_

_ {decisions.<entry>} the id of the option selected for the_

_ decision an entry of the output's_

_ decisions names, with <entry> written_

_ exactly as the entry is, as in_

_ {decisions.subanalysis.decision1}_

_ {inputs} the paths of all the output's inputs, in_

_ the order of inputs, separated by spaces_

_ {output} the path the result is written to_

__

Every brace belongs to a {{, a }} or a placeholder, every placeholder takes one of these forms, and the <entry> of an {inputs.<entry>} or {decisions.<entry>} is an entry of the output's inputs or decisions, exactly as written.

items.title: Slot: conforms_to
items.text: The IRI of the specification of the fragment syntax value follows, as W3C Web Annotation gives it, such as http://tools.ietf.org/rfc/rfc7111 for a CSV. Without it, value is a PDF fragment identifier (RFC 8118).

items.title: Slot: cpus
items.text: CPU cores requested. Fractional values are allowed (e.g., 0.5) for runners that support CPU shares.

items.title: Slot: decision
items.text: The address of the decision, written as its key in the universe's decisions.

items.title: Slot: derived_from
items.text: The id of another universe of the analysis, never an import, whose effective selection this universe's effective selection is built on, so that this universe gives only the decisions it changes. The universe inherits only that selection.

items.title: Slot: disk
items.text: Disk requirement as a string with units (e.g., '10Gi', '500Mi').

items.title: Slot: doi
items.text: The DOI name of the cited work, under the 10 directory: 10., the registrant code, / and a non-empty suffix, such as 10.5555/12345678.

items.title: Slot: entry
items.text: The entry exactly as the output's inputs lists it in the astra.yaml files at the record's commit, such as input1.

items.title: Slot: environment
items.text: The environment the recipe ran in.

items.title: Slot: evidence
items.text: What the claim rests on, as a list. There is at least one.

items.title: Slot: exact
items.text: The passage, exactly as the cited work or output writes it.

items.title: Slot: excluded
items.text: Why the option is ruled out. An option with a reason is excluded: no effective selection selects it.

items.title: Slot: findings
items.text: What the analysis concludes, as insights keyed by id.

items.title: Slot: finished
items.text: When the recipe finished, in UTC to the millisecond, such as 2026-10-26T14:00:02.000Z.

items.title: Slot: format
items.text: How the output's artefact is encoded, as a lowercase token: the extension of its results' files, without the leading dot, such as png, csv or parquet. Every output but a switch has one.

items.title: Slot: generated_by
items.text: The run of the recipe that made the result.

items.title: Slot: gpus
items.text: Number of GPUs

items.title: Slot: incompatible_with
items.text: The options that are never selected together with this option, among the decisions a universe uses.

items.title: Slot: insights
items.text: The ids of the prior insights that support the option.

items.title: Slot: iri
items.text: An IRI naming exactly that environment, enough for its runner, at the version the record gives, to recreate it, such as a urn: IRI (urn:example:env:sha256:…) or one in a scheme of the runner's own.

items.title: Slot: location
items.text: The place in the cited work or output the claim rests on, such as page=6.

items.title: Slot: memory
items.text: Memory requirement as a string with units (e.g., '16Gi', '512Mi', '8GB').

items.title: Slot: option
items.text: The id of the option selected for the decision.

items.title: Slot: options
items.text: The options the decision chooses between, keyed by id. There is at least one.

items.title: Slot: outputs
items.text: The artefacts the analysis makes, and its switches, keyed by id.

items.title: Slot: prefix
items.text: ~20-100 chars before for disambiguation

items.title: Slot: prior_insights
items.text: What earlier work establishes and the analysis builds on, as insights keyed by id. Options cite them in their insights.

items.title: Slot: quote
items.text: The passage of the cited work or output the claim rests on. With a location, the passage is sought within that place.

items.title: Slot: rationale
items.text: Why this decision exists

items.title: Slot: recipe
items.text: How the output is made. Every output but a switch has one.

items.title: Slot: requires
items.text: The options that are also selected wherever this option is, among the decisions a universe uses: a decision it doesn't use selects none.

items.title: Slot: resources
items.text: Compute resource requirements (cpus, memory, time_limit, …)

items.title: Slot: runner
items.text: The runner that ran the recipe.

items.title: Slot: scope
items.text: Applicability conditions

items.title: Slot: started
items.text: When the recipe started, in UTC to the millisecond, such as 2026-10-26T14:00:00.000Z.

items.title: Slot: suffix
items.text: ~20-100 chars after for disambiguation

items.title: Slot: switch
items.text: For a switch, the address of the decision whose selected option picks the case it takes, such as decision1 or stage.decision2.

items.title: Slot: target
items.text: A reference to the input, output or switch the switch is read as where the option is selected, written as an entry of an output's inputs is, such as stage.output3 or output1#u1.

items.title: Slot: time_limit
items.text: Maximum wall time as a duration string (e.g., '2h', '30m', '1h30m').

items.title: Slot: type
items.text: The kind of artefact the output is. Every output but a switch has one.

items.title: Slot: universe
items.text: For an import, the id of the universe it imports: a universe of the analysis that analysis leads to, never an import of that analysis.

items.title: Slot: universes
items.text: The universes of the analysis, and the universes of other analyses it imports, keyed by id. An import has an analysis and a universe.

items.title: Slot: url
items.text: Where git fetches another repository from, as a remote with no ASCII space or control character, in one of two forms: scheme:// and at least one character, where the scheme is an ASCII letter followed by any ASCII letters, digits, +, . and -, such as https://example.org/remote.git or file:///srv/remote.git; or scp-like, [user@]host:path, where host, path and any user are non-empty, user and host hold no /, @ or :, and the value doesn't start with a scheme and ://, such as git@example.org:remote.git. The declared analysis is the one at the top level of that repository, at commit.

items.title: Slot: value
items.text: The fragment identifier, without the leading #, such as page=6. It is non-empty, holds no ASCII space or control character and none of ", #, <, >, [, the backslash, ], ^, the backtick, {, | and }, and has % only before two hex digits.
